title: Why I Built a Voice Bot With Claude (and Not GPT-4)
summary: I built an open-source voice bot where you speak and it speaks back. The interesting decision wasn't the speech stack — it was the brain. Why Claude's instruction-following made it the right fit for a 'speak, don't format' constraint.

title: Python Gets the Credit — C and C++ Do the Work
summary: Your fast Python ML code isn't really Python — NumPy, PyTorch, and XGBoost are C and C++ underneath. Why that matters, when to drop to the low-level layer, and what C/C++ teaches you even if you write Python all day.

title: One Week, No PRD — Shipping a Lead-Alert System Under Pressure
summary: A dip in sales, an urgent ask straight from the CEO, and one week to ship — no requirements, no PRD, and the IT team on leave. What I built, what I learned about Azure Intune and app permissions, and why the hectic weeks teach the most.

title: Rules + Models — Building an Explainable Decision Engine
summary: When a recommendation touches money, 'the model said so' isn't good enough. How I combined deterministic business rules with a predictive model into one explainable decision engine — and why I kept them decoupled.

title: What Actually Moved My Regression Model
summary: Not hyperparameter magic — data and features. How expanding the dataset 2.7×, locating feature gaps, and a hybrid XGBoost + Ridge ensemble improved a fee-prediction model, especially on the highest-value cases.

title: From Datadog to Google Chat — Alerting People Actually See
summary: The best alert is the one a human sees in time to act. Why I replaced a heavyweight monitoring stack with Google Chat space alerts — cheaper, faster, and where the team already works.

title: Choosing a VLM for Noisy Documents — What Worked for Us
summary: For noisy scans, Vision-Language Models beat OCR-plus-text. In our testing Gemini 2.5 gave the best extraction accuracy and efficiency — but the only benchmark that matters is your own documents.

title: Embeddings, Interviews, and the Skill AI Can't Replace
summary: An embeddings interview question became a way to measure how someone understands and tackles a problem on their own — and why the real skill is pairing fundamentals with using AI to solve business problems.

title: Securing ML Pipelines — Key Vault, HIPAA, and Data Privacy
summary: Security is the part of ML no one demos and everyone needs. How I secure pipelines that touch health and financial data — secrets, identity, least privilege, and HIPAA by design.

title: Why I'm Starting This Blog
summary: A short note on what I'll be writing about here — building AI systems, working with messy real-world data, and where I think ML matters most.

title: Lessons From Building Document-AI Pipelines
summary: OCR, NLP, and vision-language models look clean in a demo and messy in production. Here are the lessons that actually moved accuracy and reliability.

title: Where AI Helps Most in Finance
summary: If healthcare keeps us well, finance keeps us stable. Where AI genuinely earns its keep in financial workflows — and the guardrails it demands.

title: Where I Think AI Helps Most in Healthcare
summary: Not every healthcare problem needs a model. A few places where AI genuinely earns its keep — and the guardrails that have to come with it.
